question: What is the single best way to stop infections from spreading in the hospital?
explanation: You've got this! Regular hand washing is your number one defense against passing germs around the ward. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to wash their hands so many times during a single shift?

options.A: To interrupt the physical transport of microorganisms
options.B: To keep skin cool under heavy medical gloves
options.C: To remove oils and sweat continuously
options.D: To comply strictly with hospital administrative rules

explanation: Every time you wash, you stop germs from hitching a ride from one patient to the next. Simple and life-saving! [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which type of skin germs can you easily wash away with routine hand washing?
explanation: Transient flora are just visiting! They sit on the surface of your skin from touching things, making them super easy to wash away. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h2)

question: If you touch an infected wound, what kind of germs do you mostly pick up on your hands?
explanation: Spot on! Touching patients picks up temporary (transient) germs on your outer skin that need a good wash. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h2)

question: In the chain of infection, what role do our hands most frequently play?
explanation: Think of your hands as the ultimate delivery vehicle—they carry germs right from the source to the patient. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h3)

question: How does hand washing help stop a sudden outbreak in the ward?

options.A: By sterilizing the external skin layers completely
options.B: By breaking the chain of infection transmission
options.C: By destroying the natural immune system
options.D: By eliminating all resident bacteria permanently

explanation: By washing your hands, you literally snap the chain of infection so the germs can't travel any further! [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h3)

question: What kind of hand cleaning is a must before you assist in a surgical operation?
explanation: Surgeries need extra care! A thorough surgical scrub gets rid of both surface and deeper germs to keep the theatre safe. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h4)

question: When should you use an antiseptic hand wash instead of a quick regular wash?

options.C: After arriving at the hospital ward

explanation: Whenever you're doing a clean procedure where germs shouldn't go, use an antimicrobial wash to be extra safe. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h4)

question: According to the WHO Five Moments for Hand Hygiene, what is the very first moment?
explanation: Always clean your hands right before you make contact with a patient, protecting them from outside germs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h5)

question: You just finished adjusting an IV line for a patient. Which WHO hand hygiene moment applies right after?
explanation: Even touching things around the patient like the bed or IV pole means you should clean your hands right after! [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h5)

question: How long should you scrub your hands with soap and water in the clinical ward?
explanation: Take your time! A full 40 to 60 seconds gives you enough friction to wash away dirt and stubborn microbes. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h6)

question: When using an alcohol-based hand rub, how long should you rub your hands together?

options.A: Until the hands are completely dry
options.B: Until the foam changes color completely
options.D: Until a warm sensation is felt on the skin

explanation: Keep rubbing until they're dry! That's when the alcohol finishes doing its germ-killing job. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h7)

question: When is it safe to use an alcohol-based hand rub instead of washing with water?

options.A: When preparing a surgical site on the abdomen
options.B: When caring for patients with severe diarrhea
options.C: When hands have visible blood stains
options.D: When hands are not visibly soiled with dirt

explanation: Alcohol rubs are great for clean hands, but if there's visible dirt or body fluids, you definitely need soap and water! [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h7)

question: What common skin issue do nurses often get from washing their hands constantly?
explanation: Frequent washing strips our natural oils, which is why dry, irritated skin is a classic nursing struggle. Don't forget your hand cream! [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h8)

question: Why is having cracked, dry skin on your hands a big worry for infection control?

options.A: It prevents alcohol rubs from evaporating fast enough
options.B: It increases bacterial colonization and pathogen trapping
options.C: It makes holding medical instruments painful
options.D: It causes patients to lose trust in clinical staff

explanation: Tiny cracks in dry skin love to trap germs, making them much harder to wash away. Take care of your hands, future nurse! [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h8)
